profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility is located at 14452 Franklin Avenue, Tustin, CA 92780, per public property records; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites, treating those specifications as commercially site-dependent rather than public data. Tustin, in Orange County, is a secondary Southern California interconnection point distinct from the denser Los Angeles/El Segundo submarket tracked elsewhere in this registry.

California regulators are actively reworking how large data center loads are billed and interconnected as demand grows statewide. Under SB 57 (2025), the California Public Utilities Commission opened a rate-design rulemaking in April 2026 addressing electric rate impacts of data centers and other large transmission-connected loads; the California Independent System Operator separately published a formal issue paper on large-load interconnection considerations in January 2026, part of an ongoing regulatory track covering the entire state grid, including Southern California Edison territory where Tustin sits.

reading.body:
Lumen operates this Tustin facility as part of a network-wide edge colocation product spanning more than 175 North American sites, not as a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen does not publish total megawatts, square footage, or per-building capacity for any individual facility, including Tustin; the operator discloses only that cabinet power ranges from 3 to 15 kilowatts across its portfolio, varying by site. Without published specifications, this facility cannot be ranked against hyperscale operators or assessed for its role in AI infrastructure scaling.

Tustin sits in Orange County, a secondary Southern California interconnection point within Southern California Edison territory, distinct from the denser Los Angeles and El Segundo submarkets tracked elsewhere. California regulators are actively reworking data center rate design and large-load interconnection rules through SB 57 and CAISO proceedings as of early 2026, creating regulatory uncertainty for any new load in the state. The state has 103 mapped data center facilities, only 11 of which publish capacity figures, totaling 365 MW of disclosed capacity.

A carrier-neutral colocation model designed for cabinet-level tenants differs fundamentally from the hyperscale GPU-dense infrastructure that drives AI scaling. Even if this site hosts AI workloads, Lumen's commercial model treats capacity as site-dependent rather than transparent, placing it outside the universe of campuses that can be evaluated against the constraint thesis. Without published power and cooling specifications from the operator, this facility does not enter the calculation of whether grid capacity binds AI deployment in California or the region.
